# Yield-curve trades

Trades: US 2s10s steepener, US 5s30s steepener, US 2s5s10s fly, DE 2s10s steepener, DE 5s20s steepener, DE 2s5s10s fly, GB 2s10s steepener, GB 5s20s steepener, GB 2s5s10s fly.  Month-end GSW, Bundesbank and Bank of England zero curves; signals formed at month-end t are traded with a one-month delay (held from t+1 to t+2), so curve-fitting noise cannot reach the return.  Evaluation 1980-01 – 2026-08 (signal dates).  Each trade risk-scaled by its 36-month volatility, equal-risk average across trades.

| policy | 560 | 1980-01 | +0.25 | +1.74 | 0.064 | +0.22 | +0.20 | +0.36 | 2.19 | 0.56 | -0.40 |
| combo | 560 | 1980-01 | +0.49 | +3.40 | 0.018 | +0.39 | +0.30 | +0.70 | 1.38 | 0.57 | -0.46 |

Placebo p: share of 1,000 random circular time shifts of each trade's positions with an equal or higher Sharpe ratio.  Costs: 0.5 / 1 bp per unit of spread DV01 traded (a 0.25 / 0.5 bp half-spread on each of two legs).  "SR, no delay" trades at the signal month-end and is exposed to curve-fitting noise.

## Multiple-testing correction across the five signals

Hansen SPA test of the null that no signal has a positive mean return (stationary bootstrap, mean block 12 months, 2,000 draws):

- from 1980: consistent p = 0.001, Reality Check p = 0.001 (best signal: combo)
- from 1990: consistent p = 0.014, Reality Check p = 0.014 (best signal: combo)

## Is it fitting noise? US check on an independent curve

Signals from GSW; returns re-measured on the Treasury's constant-maturity curve (a separate fit), with roll-down.  If GSW fitting noise drove the results, they would vanish on CMT returns.
